title: Preserve sitemap sections when the five remaining legacy readers fail on transport

source.ref: Five remaining swallowed reads named in LIVE-331 and revalidated during SCAN-1051

detail: After the scoped organizer repair, getTopicalChannels,getPublicCircles,listSitemapEventEntries,listPublicJourneys and getSpotlightRoutes/listPublishedSpotlightHandles still discard resolved transport failures or catch them as empty. LIVE331 explicitly named these as outside its closed repair. A sectionRead wrapper alone cannot help a lower reader that resolves[]; change the actual reporting boundary deliberately, preserving other callers' documented behavior and the public visibility/publish/privacy gates. Use the existing transient classifier so real PostgREST codes remain deterministic even at5xx. Keep intentional sitemap caps and their observability separate; no pagination scope expansion is inferred. Tests must drive each actual reader through a scripted SDK and the sitemap, proving healthy empty, deterministic errors and transport preservation. No migration, public privilege expansion, production outage injection or release is authorized. Repair: each reader has an explicit failClosed opt-in used only by the sitemap; legacy callers preserve their fallback behavior. Channels/circles/events/journeys pass through sectionRead and Spotlight through failSection. All strict reads reuse the existing discover retry/classifier; event catches rethrow only in strict mode. Query columns, public/publish predicates, caps, folds and handle filtering remain unchanged.154tests across5files pass, including33new actual-reader+sitemap cases; all5silent-fallbackcontrols fail as intended. Wholetyping and artifact/release acceptance are separately tracked, not implied by this source/SDK proof.

verify.note: Actual five reader bodies and shared retry/classifier/section helpers; healthy empty quiet, deterministic42501at503 stays section-local, resolved503/network and thrown fetch exhaust the existing ladder and abandon regeneration. Five in-memory silent-fallback controls fail at expected rejection. Full actual-sitemap/scriptedSDK suite154tests across5files passes; no deployed cache/search claim.
